records.notes: Writer/writing participle, or kaataba: corresponded with (Form III); the internal long vowel is retained in the stem.
Written; also a written item, letter or allotted fate. Participial noun/adjective distinction is contextual.
School (madrasa), or female teacher (mudarrisa), or a taught/studied feminine referent (mudarrasa). Feminine-ending granularity is not fixed by the contract.
Key/instrument noun; m- and the internal long vowel belong to the derived stem.
Seeking forgiveness, Form X verbal noun; the derivational initial letters are retained in the stem.
Extractor (mustakhrij), extracted thing/document (mustakhraj), or attributive participle; vowels determine the reading.
Reader/reading active participle. The radical hamza is written bare in the root.
Reading/recitation verbal noun; final ة may be kept within the lexical stem or separated under the contract's unspecified feminine convention.
Believer/believing (mu'min), securing/insuring (mu'ammin), secured/insured (mu'amman), or the established personal name. Initial m- is derivational, not a clitic.
Responsible/answerable/asked; also an official. The seated hamza in the surface is a bare hamza radical in the root.
Questioner/beggar from سأل; flowing or a liquid from سال يسيل. These homographs have distinct roots.
Principles/beginnings (plural of مبدأ), or an initiator/initiating person (mubaadi' from بادأ). Same radical root across these readings.
Speaker/saying from قال يقول, or taking a midday rest from قال يقيل. The second is a classical lexical reading.
Said/uttered (maquul), or a tongue/eloquent speaker (miqwal). Keep the word whole; the final letters are not a plural ending.
Balance/scale: initial weak radical و surfaces as ي within the instrument pattern.
Appointment/promised time: initial weak radical و surfaces as ي within the derived form.
Caller/inviter, or a motive/cause; indefinite defective participle داعٍ with the final ي absent in this spelling.
Supplication/calling, or the established personal name Duaa. Final surface hamza is derived from the weak radical و.
Archer/throwing (raamin) from رمى; sought/attempted (raama) from رام يروم. Lane also records a tree noun رام under روم. Foreign name/acronym readings are outside this set.
Thrown/targeted or a targeted person/thing; the final ي belongs to the weak-root participle and is not a possessive clitic.
Teacher (mudarris), taught/studied (mudarras), or place of study (madras); pattern vowels are not supplied.
Extended/lengthened, including a substantivized referent; doubled radical د is retained twice in the root.
Strong/severe; noun is accepted for a substantivized strong/severe person or thing. Radical د is doubled.
Preparedness/readiness, Form X verbal noun of استعد; geminate root عدد.
Earthquake/shaking, with reduplicated quadriliteral root زلزل; no separate surface affix.
Rolling (mudahrij) or rolled (mudahraj), with quadriliteral root دحرج.
Rolling, quadriliteral verbal noun; final ة has alternative lexical/feminine span treatments.

Tranquillity. Synchronic طمءن, metathesized طءمن and the traditional triliteral lexicographic treatment طمن are retained as disputed analyses, not equally settled alternatives. Human adjudication of the root policy is needed.
Sparrows/small birds, broken plural of عصفور; also lexical metaphorical senses. The traditional root entry is quadriliteral عصفر.
Men, or people on foot (plural of راجل). Broken plural remains one stem; adjective permits the on-foot reading.
Houses/rooms, a broken plural of بيت. Internal و is part of the plural pattern.
Mosques/places of prostration, broken plural; no external plural suffix.
Keys, broken plural of مفتاح; the final يح is not a suffix.
Books (kutub), wrote/was written (kataba/kutiba), or Form II kattaba/kuttiba and imperative kattib when shadda/vowels are omitted.
Knowledge/science (ilm), flag/landmark (alam), knew (alima), or taught/marked (allama) and related unvocalized verbal forms.
Gold (dhahab) or went (dhahaba), including Form II gilded when shadda is omitted.
Promise/promised, or the personal name Waad. Also و + عَدّ / عَدَّ (and counting / and he counted), or و + عِدْ (and promise!). Bare initial و therefore need not be a radical.
Said (قول), or took a midday rest (قيل). A lexical noun قال meaning speech/gossip is also attested; no generic quotation-only noun reading is assumed.
Sold (بيع), armspan (بوع), or stretched/measured by armspan (بوع). Distinct weak radicals matter.
Threw; weak final ي appears as alif maqsura. It is part of the stem.
Called/supplicated (daaa, دعو), or dual imperative دَعَا (you two leave!, ودع). Final ا is stem-final in the first and a dual subject ending in the second.
Ate/eating/food (أكل), or interrogative أ + كَلَّ (did he tire?) / كُلّ (is every/all ...?). The second root depends on a clitic reading and is less likely in isolation.
Asked (saala), or an intensive Form II reading with omitted shadda. The hamza is radical.
Read/recited; the surface final hamza is a radical.
They write/are written or Form II equivalents. Imperfective ي remains in the stem because no person-prefix span type exists; ون may be bundled or split into subject و and mood ن.
You feminine singular write, or passive/derived equivalents. ين may be bundled or split into feminine subject ي and indicative ن.
Masculine plural imperative write!. Final وا includes the orthographic alif with the plural ending; it is not assigned a separate fictitious morpheme.
For/to their school or female teacher; initial ل can also be emphatic la-. ة surfaces as ت before هم, with three plausible feminine boundary treatments.
And with/by their book; و conjunction, ب preposition, هم possessive pronoun.
So/then in the schools; مدارس can also be a Form III participle mudaAris. ف + ب + ال are separate clitics.
Our children: broken plural أطفال plus possessive نا.
Their female teachers, marked/taught feminine referents, or informing feminine referents; ات is the productive plural ending and هم is possessive.
With/in the two cars. Feminine ت may stay in the oblique-dual base سيارت, be separated, or be bundled with ين; this is a segmentation-policy ambiguity.
And the female students/seekers or feminine seeking referents; productive plural ات follows the participial stem.
Hospitals, or feminine plural healing-seeking/healed participial referents. Stem-final ي is the weak-root allomorph before ات.
Libraries/bookshops, or feminine plural of a writing-related derived participle such as مُكَتِّب. ات is a productive plural ending.
And with their book; each attached vowel/sukun stays with its preceding original letter, including at clitic boundaries.
Vocalized active Form II participle: teacher/teaching. Shadda and kasra are attached to ل inside the stem.
Vocalized passive Form II participle: taught/marked, or the person/thing so described. This differs from مُعَلِّم despite identical normalized letters.
Explicitly vocalized active perfective wrote. Diacritics constrain the POS reading even though the model does not learn vowel distinctions.
Explicitly vocalized passive perfective was written. All attached marks are covered by the stem span.
Vocalized seeking forgiveness; initial kasra is attached to ا and is not a forbidden leading mark.
Established name Muhammad, or praised/praiseworthy (muHammad), possibly substantivized. Arabic derivational root is retained for the name.
Cairo, or the feminine conqueror/overpowering one. ال is an article even in the established name; ة can remain in the lexical stem or be separated.
Borrowed proper name Ibrahim/Abraham; no invented Arabic triliteral or quadriliteral root.
Borrowed proper name Washington. Initial و belongs to the name, not a conjunction.
Two books: كتاب plus the nominative dual ending ان.
Female writers/writing feminine plural; ات is the productive sound-feminine-plural ending.
Future negator lan, or imperative lin: be soft/gentle, from لان يلين. The imperative is a grammatical inference from the cited lemma.

In; or in me (فِيَّ with omitted shadda); genitive-construct mouth (فِي) / my mouth (فِيَّ), root فوه; or feminine imperative fulfill! from وفى. Fused ي allocation is convention-sensitive. Noun/verb alternatives are classical contextual readings.

Demonstrative this, either lexical whole or attention ه + ذا. Also هَذَّا, dual perfective/imperative of هذّ (cut/recite quickly); the dual reading is an inflectional inference from the cited classical verb.
Masculine plural relative pronoun. Initial ال is lexical within the relative pronoun rather than a productive definite article.
We (naHnu), or we yearn/long (naHinnu) from حنّ. In the verbal reading the imperfective ن remains inside the stem.

I (anaa); or أَنَّا, dual of أنّ (groaned), and أَنًّا, accusative groaning verbal noun, when marks are omitted. The rare alternatives require context; final ا is dual agreement or orthographic accusative support.
Future particle sawfa; Form II sawwafa, put off/delayed, or its imperative; sawf, smelling/delaying verbal noun. Function-word reading has null root, lexical readings root سوف.
From (min), who/whoever (man), manna/favour/counting-a-favour noun (mann), or granted a favour/reproached (manna) and related geminate verbal readings. Function readings have null root.

Rejected: ASCII digits are outside arabic-v1.
Rejected: whitespace is not permitted inside one word.
Rejected: combining mark precedes any base letter.
Rejected: emoji is outside arabic-v1 (two UTF-16 code units).

limitations: Independent AI authorship is not independent human gold. No model predictions, teacher labels, generated training data, existing fixtures, or the other annotator's output were inspected.

Field-level accepted sets are partial alternatives, not a Cartesian product of mutually compatible full analyses. They do not establish exhaustive morphological correctness, natural-text accuracy, or calibrated uncertainty.

Canonical roots use bare ء for every radical hamza, explicit repeated geminate radicals, and underlying و/ي for weak radicals. Arabic-derived proper names retain a root; grammatical function-word and borrowed-name readings receive null.

Undiacritized words admit lexical, vocalic and clitic ambiguity. Common and independently identified classical readings are included, but rare vocabulary, every possible personal/place-name use, dialectal spellings, acronym/brand uses and arbitrary metalinguistic quotations are not exhaustively enumerated.
POS noun/adjective ambiguity is accepted for lexical and substantivized participles. Word-level POS follows the lexical host rather than an attached conjunction, preposition or other clitic.

The contract fixes span coverage and offsets but not morpheme granularity. Feminine ة/ت may remain in a lexical stem or use derivational_suffix/inflectional_suffix; subject suffixes may use inflectional_suffix or pronominal_enclitic. Listed variants explicitly reflect this unresolved policy.

Internal templatic and initial derivational letters remain in stem spans. Imperfective person prefixes remain in stem spans because the schema has no inflectional_prefix category. Broken plurals receive no artificial external plural suffix.

Every segmentation covers the original string in JavaScript UTF-16 code units. Attached vowels, shadda, sukun and other marks remain with their preceding letter. No normalization-folded offsets or zero-length morphemes are used.

Fused forms such as في / فِيَّ and attention ه in هذا cannot expose all underlying morphology without a surface-allocation convention; they have low confidence. The root history of طمأنينة is disputed and needs a declared lexicographic policy and human adjudication.

Pattern and feature sets are deliberately omitted. Sources support the specified lexical/grammar facts; unvocalized inflected possibilities are sometimes grammatical inferences from a cited lemma rather than exact dictionary headwords.
Confidence is an AI judgement about these partial labels, not a probability and not evidence of a human review.
